html:
The leading general of the emperor Justinian I, often counted among the great commanders of history. He came from the Balkans and won most of his victories with small armies.

  • 530: beat a larger Persian army at Dara.
  • 532: crushed the Nika riots in the Hippodrome.
  • 533 to 534: conquered the Vandal kingdom of Africa in the Vandalic War and brought its king to Constantinople.
  • 535 to 540: took Sicily, Naples and Rome, held Rome through a year-long siege and captured Ravenna in the Gothic War.

The Goths offered to make him western emperor; he pretended to accept and took the city for Justinian. The emperor never fully trusted him after that. His later campaigns in Italy went worse, and Narses finished the war. In 559 he came out of retirement to drive off raiders at the Battle of Melantias. His secretary Procopius wrote his campaigns. A later legend that he ended as a blind beggar is not true.
